title: Training: checkpoints that do not stall the GPUs
purpose: Run the same job twice, once writing checkpoints inline and once in the background, and measure how long each one stops training.

steps.display: kubectl create -f trainjob.yaml   # s04-sync: 2 nodes x 1 GPU, 120 steps, checkpoint every 30 (sync)
checkpoint events from S3, sync run (rank 0)
steps.output:
step 30: pause 2.85 s
step 60: pause 2.62 s
step 90: pause 2.14 s
step 120: pause 2.63 s
local write 0.38 s, upload to S3 1.88 s, 681.7 MB (rank 0 shard)

steps.display: kubectl create -f trainjob.yaml   # s04-async: 2 nodes x 1 GPU, 120 steps, checkpoint every 30 (async)
checkpoint events from S3, async run (rank 0)
steps.output:
step 30: pause 0.53 s
step 60: pause 0.53 s
step 90: pause 0.16 s
step 120: pause 0.16 s
local write 0.54 s, upload to S3 2.25 s, 681.7 MB (rank 0 shard)

steps.display: comparison (median pause per checkpoint, whole-run time)
steps.output:
sync  : 2.62 s per checkpoint, run took 61.3 s
async : 0.34 s per checkpoint, run took 55.4 s
async stops training 7.6x less per checkpoint

steps.display: aws s3api list-objects-v2 --prefix runs/s04-async/ckpt/step-000060/   # modified times

steps.output: async at one checkpoint every 30 steps costs 2.9% of training time in pauses (step time about 0.39 s)

checks.description: both runs completed with every checkpoint written
checks.because: Checkpoints at steps 30, 60, 90 and the final step, from both ranks.

checks.description: asynchronous checkpointing stops training at least 3 times less than writing inline
checks.because: Async pauses only for the device-to-host copy; the disk write and the S3 upload run on a background thread.

checks.description: the background upload really did take longer than the pause (the work moved off the training path)
checks.because: Write plus upload took several times the pause the training loop saw.

checks.description: a checkpoint's completion marker is written after its shard, so a half-written checkpoint is never chosen
checks.because: The loader accepts a step only when every rank's marker exists, and markers are written last.
